xref_precision and xref_recall of a tags-engine tool format score the file resolver's file-resolved edges (fusion.ResolveFileEdges over the dialect's import strategy, the edges ingest stores) against the oracle's cross_references at file granularity: (file, referring definition, referenced file), the referenced definition's name not compared (LB-F56)

universal-ctags 6.2.1 (tier B, unscored second oracle) over all 195 apache/thrift files: 6,254 of the dialect's 6,796 definitions match at equal kind and within two lines (ctags reports 6,480). The dialect-only 542 are 234 namespaces (ctags names a namespace by its value, the dialect by its scope), 225 consts and 68 fields ctags does not tag, 15 others; the ctags-only 226 are 223 namespaces and 3 enum values ctags mis-tokenizes (hex-style names).

thrift --gen json carries no source positions and writes a typedef's target where a member names the typedef: calibration/oracles/thrift-json places declarations and type names with its own scanner and refuses a file unless the scanner equals the compiler's definitions and non-typedef references (see its README). apache/thrift: 8 files the compiler rejects (include no root holds, BrokenConstants.thrift, a Rust test's missing includes) contribute nothing.
disposition: met: target L3, met L3 excellent (wave lang7, fathom 9c3cf0ef2) on apache/thrift v0.24.0 (187 of 195 files: the compiler rejects 8) and jaegertracing/jaeger-idl v0.14.0 (4 files): L1 excellent (sym_recall 1, sym_precision 1, 6,832 definitions, 6,832 of 6,832 ranges), L2 excellent (ref_recall 1, ref_precision 1, 2,242 pairs), L3 excellent (xref_precision 1, xref_recall .9574, 45 of 47 cross-file references) against the Apache Thrift compiler 0.24.0 (tier A for the definition and reference sets; positions and typedef-name references are the harness scanner's, held to the compiler file by file). The 2 missed cross-file references: a name two included files both define (jaeger-idl's agent.thrift includes jaeger.thrift and zipkincore.thrift, which each define Span: the file resolver binds a qualified type through the names the includes bring into scope and no file-symbol parameter reads the qualifier, so an ambiguous name binds nothing, never the wrong file, O1443) and a type whose name starts in lower case (apache/thrift's test/py/explicit_module/test2.thrift names test1.astruct: the resolver keeps a wildcard-bound name only when it starts upper case). Holdout (apache/impala 4.5.2, pinned before any reading, read once): docs/bench/readings/lang/holdout/thrift.json.
